gloss: either one; one or the other

definitions.gloss: either one; one or the other; which one
definitions.explanation: A colloquial contraction of どちらか, used when choosing between two options. Can function as a question ('which one?') or as a statement ('one of the two').

examples.japanese: どっちかと{言|い}えば、{映画|えいが}のほうが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: If I had to choose, I'd say I prefer movies.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}と{青|あお}のどっちかにしてくれない？どっちでもいいから{早|はや}く{決|き}めてよ。
examples.english: Can you pick either the red one or the blue one? I don't care which, so just decide quickly.

notes:
A colloquial contraction of どちらか (which one of the two; either one). Very common in casual spoken Japanese. The full form どちらか is used in polite or formal speech.

The expression どっちかと{言|い}えば (if I had to say which; if anything) is an extremely common hedging phrase used to express a mild preference.

USAGE:
- どっちか{選|えら}んで: pick one (of two)
- どっちかと{言|い}えば: if I had to choose; if anything
- どっちかに{決|き}める: to decide on one or the other

RELATED WORDS:
- どちらか: either one — the polite/formal equivalent
- どっち: which one (of two) — the informal question form without か
- どれか: any one (of three or more) — for selecting from more than two options
- どちら: which one (of two) — the polite form of どっち
